cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Calm About the Impossible
cards.instruction: Remain perfectly calm around impossible events while becoming increasingly alarmed by ordinary details.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your dragon can stay for tea. Brush the biscuit crumbs onto a plate, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His three heads breathe fire. Should I take him outside?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He can stay. Three mouths, though—why have we only laid one napkin? Set two more places immediately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He brought three paper napkins. I'll use those.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put them away! Linen at this table. Fetch three matching ones, and please don't unfold them with biscuit on your fingers.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects napkin count and A5 linen handling, escalating ordinary table alarm while calmly accepting B2 fire-breathing guest.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 three heads causes extra settings; B4 three paper napkins causes A5 rejection of material and matching linen demand.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers to move a dangerous guest out and B4 supplies a useful napkin solution, practical contributions.

heightening.evidence: A5 becomes alarmed by B4 mundane material rather than the accepted fire, developing the same inverted priorities.

specificity.evidence: A1 tea and crumbs, B2 dragon heads/fire and A3 napkin count establish the hosting problem.

brevityWit.evidence: A1 now gives the crumb instruction without explaining A's expertise; A5 fingers warning recalls the established biscuit handling.
